--- a/base58/__init__.py
+++ b/base58/__init__.py
@@ -105,6 +105,7 @@
-    # Valid characters and a bytes.translate table mapping each character
-    # to its digit value (None if some digit value does not fit in a byte)
-    invmap = _get_base58_decode_map(alphabet, autofix=autofix)
-    if max(invmap.values(), default=0) > 255:
-        return bytes(invmap), None
-    return bytes(invmap), bytes(invmap.get(c, 0) for c in range(256))
+    # Valid characters and a bytes.translate table mapping each character
+    # to its digit value and every invalid character to 255 (None if some
+    # digit value does not fit below 255)
+    invmap = _get_base58_decode_map(alphabet, autofix=autofix)
+    if max(invmap.values(), default=0) >= 255:
+        return bytes(invmap), None
+    return bytes(invmap), bytes(invmap.get(c, 255) for c in range(256))

--- a/base58/__init__.py
+++ b/base58/__init__.py
@@ -126,8 +126,12 @@
-    invalid = v.translate(None, valid)
-    if invalid:
-        raise ValueError("Invalid character {!r}".format(chr(invalid[0])))
-    if table is None:
-        map = _get_base58_decode_map(alphabet, autofix=autofix)
-        digits = [map[char] for char in v]
-    else:
-        digits = v.translate(table)
+    if table is None:
+        invalid = v.translate(None, valid)
+        if invalid:
+            raise ValueError("Invalid character {!r}".format(chr(invalid[0])))
+        map = _get_base58_decode_map(alphabet, autofix=autofix)
+        digits = [map[char] for char in v]
+    else:
+        # Invalid characters translate to 255, which no digit uses
+        digits = v.translate(table)
+        if 255 in digits:
+            bad = v[digits.index(255)]
+            raise ValueError("Invalid character {!r}".format(chr(bad)))

actions.reason: b58decode_int validated input with v.translate(None, valid) before translating it to digits. That call rebuilds a 256-entry deletion table every time, on top of the second translate pass. The cached translate table now maps every invalid byte to 255, a value no digit can take. Validation becomes a single memchr-backed `255 in digits` check on the bytes that were already translated. The first invalid character is found with digits.index(255), so the error message names the same character as before. If an alphabet has a digit value of 255 or more (256 or more entries), the code falls back to the original path with the old validation unchanged. Equivalence harness: identical outputs. Measured: decode_ir ratio 0.983, check_ir ratio 0.992, encode_ir ratio 1.0005 (unchanged code path).
